Hypothetical future L2s will. Fair Hi Team - For the merge testing of testnets, I would like to volunteer as well. Is this the right place to reach out? Hey Team, just to confirm, we still need to use lighthouse's unstable branch for Ropsten nodes right? We can use stable branch only after mainnet merge? you should use `stable` branch for ropsten Obviously, `eth_getWork` (and other pow-related methods) is deprecated by the Merge, though, there is no proposal on making this deprecation into the spec. I haven't seen any proposals on renaming `eth_coinbase` either do someone know how to checkpoint-sync kiln? i am trying to sync a node on lighthouse but it is going at 3 slot/sec I can give you a lighthouse endpoint if you need it for checkpoint sync Minor addendum: if the core protocol was able to deliver execution sharding on time, users wouldn't have to be exposed to so called "centralised/controlled" L2s. And guess what? With every delay of the merge (for security reasons, ofc 😉), resulting in delay of Shanghai and 4844, L2s will be forced to switch to third party DA layers instead of eth L1 to settle data txs, to cut down on fees. Third party DA layers which are "centralised/controlled". And once again, we will blame these third party protocols for being less safe instead of looking in the mirror and reflecting that the core L1 roadmap being unable to deliver on time gave rise to these insecure outsourcings in the first place Gas is 16 gwei with diff bomb going off what’s the problem here 😅 so if the L2s are mostly all still uprgradeable/centralized/etc... why the rush for 4844. Shouldn't we prioritize getting withdrawals working and any merge cleanup asap before worrying about L2 data (not even mentioning how low fees are now as Chs2 said) Can you move this to <#595721451651465227>, as it's not really on topic for the merge anymore. Thanks!

excerpts.author: syentist.
excerpts.content: Minor addendum: if the core protocol was able to deliver execution sharding on time, users wouldn't have to be exposed to so called "centralised/controlled" L2s. And guess what? With every delay of the merge (for security reasons, ofc 😉), resulting in delay of Shanghai and 4844, L2s will be forced to switch to third party DA layers instead of eth L1 to settle data txs, to cut down on fees. Third party DA layers which are "centralised/controlled". And once again, we will blame these third party protocols for being less safe instead of looking in the mirror and reflecting that the core L1 roadmap being unable to deliver on time gave rise to these insecure outsourcings in the first place
